Mail3D
The native 3D e-mail client, sitting beside Agenda3D / Contact3D in the same JVM.
MailAccount
One configured IMAP/SMTP account: the connection endpoints, the login, the transport security, the outgoing signature, and how the password is handled.
MailAccount.CredentialMode
Where the password comes from.
MailAccount.Security
How the transport is secured.
MailAccountStore
Persists the configured MailAccounts under the /mail/accounts Preferences node - one child node per account - and owns the sealed password of any account in MailAccount.CredentialMode.SAVED mode (via CredentialVault).
MailAddress
A single RFC-822 mailbox: an optional display name plus an e-mail address.
MailAttachment
One attachment on a MailMessage: its file name, MIME type and size, plus (optionally) the bytes.
MailBackendException
The single checked failure the MailService backend reports, wrapping a jakarta.mail.MessagingException (or an I/O error) in a mail-domain exception so the UI never has to import Jakarta Mail types.
MailFolder
A mailbox folder on one account: its (server) name, its role, and the counts the folder tree shows beside it.
MailFolder.Type
The well-known roles a folder can play.
MailMessage
A single e-mail message: the shared, Java 3D-free model both the 2D MailPanel and the native-3D Mail3D render, and the value object the MailService backend maps to and from the wire (Jakarta Mail).
MailPanel
The 2D/Swing mail client: a real, configurable IMAP/SMTP front end built on the shared MailSessionManager / MailService model it also shares with the native-3D Mail3D.
MailRule
A user-defined filter: when a fetched message's from, subject or to matches a condition, an action (move / mark-read / flag / delete) is applied.
MailRule.Action
What happens to a message that matches.
MailRule.Field
Which header the condition inspects.
MailRule.Match
How the field is compared against the value.
MailRuleStore
Persists the ordered list of MailRules under the /mail/rules Preferences node - one child node per rule.
MailService
The mail backend contract both desktops program against.
MailSessionManager
Owns the live MailService sessions for every configured account and the cross-cutting behaviour both desktops share: credential resolution, connection caching / reconnect, applying the user's MailRules to freshly fetched mail, an optional periodic auto-check, and a "test connection" probe for the account dialog.
MailSessionManager.PasswordPrompt
Supplies a password interactively for ASK-mode accounts.
MailSessionManager.ServiceFactory
Creates the backend for an account; injectable so tests use a fake.
MailSettings
The user-customizable appearance and behaviour of the mail client, persisted under the /mail/settings Preferences node.
MailSettings.Density
Row spacing in the message list.
MailSettings.ReadingPanePosition
Where the reading pane sits relative to the message list.
MailSettings.SortColumn
The column the list sorts by on open.
MailSettings.Theme
Overall color theme.
MailView
The native 3D mail client's main surface, rasterised entirely at runtime into a single live texture (the Histogram3D / AgendaGrid recipe): a message list on the left and a reading / quick-reply pane on the right, under a slim account / folder header.
MailView.MailListener
Notified when a click selects a message in the list.
